defects.title: hooks.accept / hooks.leaf_slots forwarding is pinned by NO test — the whole 883-test suite stays green when the accept= forward is deleted
defects.failure_scenario: Measured, not hypothesised. In a sandbox copy of the worktree I changed gp.py's `accept=hooks.accept if hooks is not None else None,` to `accept=None,` and ran the complete suite: 883 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed — unchanged. Same for `leaf_slots=hooks.leaf_slots if hooks is not None else None)` -> `leaf_slots=None)`. (The other 16 mutations I tried all go red: DF ban key validated against minute fields, unconditional daily append in view_cache_key, daily=None in GPMiner, report.generations=n_gen, stopped_early blanked, mine()-level wall_seconds ignored, daily_fields/op_weight not forwarded, FITNESS_KINDS guard restored, make_scorer without dates/warmup, no _DEFAULT reset, register() not called, declare_real_valued rebinding, search_hooks_from first-wins, wall-clock check removed, wall-clock check without the short-circuit.) The accept hook is the single most load-bearing lever of 乙 — it is how Partura's reverse guidance (WP11) thins candidates. If any later edit or merge drops that one line (WP8 touches the same constructor's call site region), every "steer" arm silently runs unsteered, every steer-vs-control comparison becomes invalid, and no test fails. The test file's own docstring waives the coverage on an unsound premise: "The other four SearchHooks fields forward through the identical `hooks.X if hooks is not None else <default>` line op_weight does" — they are five SEPARATE lines, each independently breakable. I verified the implementation is correct today: hooks=SearchHooks(accept=...) reaches generator.accept_hook (40/40 calls) and really filters (no O:cs_rank survived in a 40-tree population, while a control population without the hook contains it).
defects.suggested_fix: Add two assertions in the style of the op_weight test (which is non-vacuous and does go red): (1) `m = GPMiner(..., hooks=SearchHooks(accept=lambda e: 'O:cs_rank' not in e.key()))`, then assert `m.generator.accept_hook is not None` and that no tree in `m.generator.generate_population(40)` carries that key, with a plain-miner control that does carry it; (2) `slots = {'div': {0: ('Amt',)}}; assert GPMiner(..., hooks=SearchHooks(leaf_slots=slots)).generator.leaf_slots is slots`. Both are ~6 lines and cost no runtime.

defects.title: The daily fingerprint reaches only the GP branch's ExemplarCache key; the RL branch still keys the same daily-aware view the old way, so the two now fight over one cache root
defects.failure_scenario: gp.py now passes `daily=dailyfields.fingerprint(getattr(view.store, "daily", None))` into view_cache_key, but pipeline.py:416 (the RL/BatchRewarder branch) still calls `view_cache_key(view, rank_ban.index.days.size, rank_ban.index.cols.size)` with no `daily=`. For one and the same daily-aware view the GP key and the RL key therefore differ, and `ExemplarCache.__init__` -> `_drop_other_views()` (rankban.py:182-191) rmtree's every directory that is not the current key. Measured on a synthetic cube with a daily root attached: GP-style key 808c024d0c2c22e5 vs plain/RL-style key 83ec29e98a002927; constructing the second cache reported dropped_views=1 and the next GP construction came back with hits=0 after having had hits=3. So a sweep that alternates a GP arm and an RL arm against the same --exemplar-cache root under --daily-fields re-pays the full ban-archive fingerprint install on every switch — the design itself measures that at 1h-2h04m for 1049-1673 exemplars, i.e. the exact cost this cache exists to avoid. The stale-fingerprint hazard WP7 set out to close also stays open on the RL half. WP8's step list (design "### WP8") never mentions this line, so it will not be fixed by accident.
defects.suggested_fix: WP8 owns pipeline.py; its step list needs one more item: at pipeline.py:416 pass the same argument the GP path passes — `view_cache_key(view, rank_ban.index.days.size, rank_ban.index.cols.size, daily=dailyfields.fingerprint(getattr(view.store, "daily", None)))` (lazy `from .dailyfields import fingerprint`). Nothing in WP7 needs to change; flag it into WP8's scope so the two branches cannot diverge.

defects.title: After a wall-clock stop the trailing _roll still labels its block with the PLANNED generation count, contradicting the report.generations fix in the same run
defects.failure_scenario: `self._roll(population, raw, n_gen)` after the loop passes the planned n_gen as the block's `generation`, and `_roll` puts it straight into the dict handed to on_block (gp.py:564). pipeline.py:336 prints `=== 第 i 块结束(至第 {info['generation']} 代)===` and pipeline.py:343 writes `{"index": i, "generation": info["generation"]}` into the run's block log. Measured: a rolling_block=2, ban_top_n=1 run with wall_seconds=1e-9 and a 6-generation budget returns report.generations=1 / stopped_early='wall clock' while the block entry says generation=6. The same run meta then states two different generation counts — which is the very confusion must_fix #6 fixed for report.generations.
defects.suggested_fix: `self._roll(population, raw, done_gen or n_gen)` on gp.py:827 (done_gen is already in scope and is >= 1 whenever the loop ran).

defects.title: Negative wall_seconds silently means "stop after one generation", NaN silently means "never stop"
defects.failure_scenario: `self.wall_seconds = float(wall_seconds)` accepts any float. Measured: GPMiner(wall_seconds=-1.0).mine(8*5) returns generations=1, stopped_early='wall clock' (-1.0 is truthy and `elapsed >= -1` is true at the first check), and GPMiner(wall_seconds=float('nan')).mine(8*3) runs the full 3 generations with stopped_early='' (NaN is truthy, every `>=` comparison is False). WP8 will wire this to a `--wall-seconds` CLI flag, where `--wall-seconds -1` (or a shell variable that expanded to `nan`/empty-then-minus) silently truncates a production run to one generation and still writes a normal-looking archive.
defects.suggested_fix: In __init__: `ws = float(wall_seconds); if not math.isfinite(ws) or ws < 0: raise ValueError("wall_seconds must be a finite number >= 0"); self.wall_seconds = ws` (math is already imported), and apply the same coercion to mine()'s override argument.

defects.title: rankban.view_cache_key's new docstring promises invalidation on a daily-field rebuild that fingerprint() cannot deliver (meta.json is hashed, plane values are not)
defects.failure_scenario: The docstring ends "日频数据重建后旧的秩指纹不会被错误地当成仍然有效". dailyfields.fingerprint is `f"{DERIVED_VERSION}:{store.meta_sha256}"` and meta_sha256 = _sha256_file(meta.json), i.e. the fields/symbols/dates manifest only. Measured: rewriting daily_FloatCap.npy with doubled values over the same symbols/dates/fields gives the IDENTICAL fingerprint (1:91df5161...), hence the identical cache key, hence stale rank fingerprints served as valid and a rank ban that refuses the wrong candidates — the exact failure the sentence claims is closed. The production path is saved by accident: scripts/build_daily_fields.py puts built_at/coverage into meta.json, so a full rebuild through it does move the hash; a hand-patched plane, or a directory written by synthetic.write_daily_fields (which writes only fields/symbols/dates), does not. The repo test even states the limitation in a comment (tests/test_plugin_hooks.py:422-425) while the docstring states the opposite.
defects.suggested_fix: Either weaken the docstring to what is true ("只要 meta.json 变了就会换键 —— 生产的 build_daily_fields.py 会写 built_at/coverage,所以整目录重建一定换键;手工改 .npy 而不动 meta.json 不会"), or make it true by hashing the plane bytes in dailyfields.fingerprint (WP1/WP2's file, e.g. mix in each daily_<name>.npy's size+mtime+sha256-of-first-N-bytes).

result.notes:
Suite line (worktree, full run): 883 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 128.26s (0:02:08). Baseline was 617/10/1; no new failures, no skips added.

WHAT CHECKS OUT (design step by step, verified against source, not taken on trust)
- Owned-file discipline: `git show --stat HEAD` = exactly plugins.py (new), mining/gp.py, mining/rankban.py, tests/test_plugin_hooks.py. `git status --porcelain` empty. Commit title starts with "WP7:", last line is the required Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5.
- Steps 1-9 are all present with the signatures the design names. SearchHooks fields/defaults, load_plugins (import -> register() if callable -> unconditional `catalog._DEFAULT = None` iff anything loaded -> returns names), declare_real_valued (`.update`, in place), search_hooks_from (last wins, None otherwise). Both required docstring caveats ("AlphaCube never imports a plugin on its own", "a caller holding an already-returned Registry still sees the short vocabulary") are there.
- DEFAULT-PATH IDENTITY, the strongest check I could build: I ran a default-argument GPMiner (seed 5, pop 10, max_depth 3, 3 generations) against the SAME on-disk synthetic store from the read-only baseline tree (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube, 517fd09) and from this worktree, dumping registry size, the 214 spec names, every generation's bred population keys, the archive, and the report. 308-line digests are byte-identical (script: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP7/xtree_run.py). So the whole WP1-WP7 stack, WP7's five new generator keywords included, leaves the random stream and the results untouched at the defaults, and report.generations == n_gen when nothing stops early.
- `hooks=None` vs `hooks=SearchHooks()`: SearchHooks.leaf_slots defaults to `{}` where TypedTreeGenerator defaults to `None`, so plugins.py:45's claim "Every field's default is exactly the value TypedTreeGenerator itself defaults to" is not literally true — but generator.py:574 is the only reader and it tests `if self.leaf_slots else None`, so `{}` and `None` are behaviourally identical. Harmless; the dataclass matches the design's own spec. Side effect of the dict field: `hash(SearchHooks())` raises TypeError although frozen=True suggests hashability (`==` works, which is what the tests use).
- Wall clock: `ws` falsy at the default short-circuits before time.perf_counter(); I confirmed the dedicated test is real by mutating the check to evaluate its second operand unconditionally (goes red). mine(wall_seconds=None) defers to the constructor, mine(wall_seconds=0) disables a constructor value, budget < population_size still reports 1 generation, done_gen cannot stay 0 (the loop has no early continue/break before `done_gen = g + 1`).
- DF ban keys: one_layer_keys really emits `O:cs_rank(DF:FloatCap)` (verified by parsing), the new branch sits before `F:` and cannot shadow it, `O:nt_ts_argmax(DF:FloatCap)|w3` and mixed `O:div(DF:FloatCap,F:Amt)` pass, `DF:floatcap` is rejected. End to end: banning the most frequent real daily key (`O:pow_3(DF:FloatCap)`, 10 occurrences in 400 unbanned trees) drops it to 0 occurrences.
- Exemplar cache: with no daily root attached fingerprint() is None and the hashed string is byte-identical (hand-written-hash test goes red if the append is made unconditional); with a root attached the key is stable across store reopens, so a second run hits the cache (hits=3/3).
- fitness_kind/make_scorer: scorer_kinds() is a superset of FITNESS_KINDS, built-in kinds reach PanelScorer/LongScorer with exactly today's arguments (make_scorer does not forward dates/warmup to them), a registered kind receives dates=list(view.dates) and the warmup given, and the ValueError text names the full list.
- No import cycle: `alphacube.plugins` imports cleanly first, and `alphacube.mining.gp` first works too. `default_registry()` is the only registry cache and it is lazy, so `_DEFAULT = None` is sufficient.

SMALLER OBSERVATIONS I did not file as defects
- mine()'s t0 is taken before `_add_exemplars(self._pending_exemplars)`, which the design measures at 1-2 hours for a large ban archive. A --wall-seconds smaller than the install time therefore stops the run after exactly one generation. That is what the design asked for (reuse t0), but WP8's CLI help should say the clock covers the exemplar install.
- gp.py:53 still defines its own `FITNESS_KINDS = ("ic","rank_ic","long","long_hit")`, now unreferenced in that file. Nothing imports it today, but it is a trap for WP8: a stale duplicate that will silently drift from scoring.FITNESS_KINDS. Deleting it (or re-exporting scoring's) is a one-liner.
- search_hooks_from calls `search_hooks()` on EVERY module that exposes one and keeps the last result (side effects of the discarded ones still run), does not type-check the result (a plugin returning a dict surfaces later as `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'op_weight'` inside GPMiner.__init__), and a later module whose search_hooks() returns None wipes an earlier module's hooks. All defensible readings of "last module wins".
- A failed import mid-list (`load_plugins(["good","typo"])`) raises after the good module's register() already ran and before the `_DEFAULT` reset, leaving the cached registry stale and the new kernel invisible to default_registry(). Hard-error path; the CLI dies anyway.
- SearchHooks(daily_fields=...) is never validated against registry.daily_fields. Measured: a typo'd name generates `cross_mean(FlaotCap, 60)` and every such candidate scores -inf instead of raising, so `daily_leaf_prob=1.0` plus one typo yields a run that finds nothing and says nothing. The draw site is WP5's generator, but SearchHooks is the natural place to catch it.
- `getattr(view.store, "daily", None)` tolerates a store without `.daily` but needs the view to have `.store`; a duck-typed view (no in-repo caller does this) would now raise AttributeError in GPMiner.__init__. This is verbatim what the design prescribed.
